task: Build Drink Stand v1, the third minigame of the esl-likes 3D ESL game, as a complete playable slice: fixed-camera 3D drink stand, customers arrive at serving windows, the child asks 'What drink do you like?', hears 'I like ___.', pours the right drink from one of six stations and serves it, with levels, patience, streaks, a RUSH finale and the turnaround. The shared shell, speech stack, Restaurant and Coloring already exist and work; this order adds one minigame against the frozen interface.
requirements: Read SPEC.md first: the anti-shortcut rule near the top, section 3 ('Listening again'), and section 6 (Drink Stand v1), which is the frozen design and wins over any assumption. Read DESIGN_DECISIONS.md for existing rationale. Do not modify SPEC.md.

Create src/minigames/drinkStand/ with at least index.js (createDrinkStand(ctx) controller), scoring.js (PURE logic, no DOM, no three.js) and scoring.test.mjs (node:test). Further modules in that folder are welcome (world building, customer queue).

createDrinkStand(ctx) implements the frozen interface { id, enter(level), update(dt), exit() } exactly as src/minigames/restaurant/index.js does, including the same level resolution (enter(level) falling back to settings 'difficulty', clamped 1..3) and the settings subscription for micFree / textSize.

Register it: src/main.js minigames map gets ['drink-stand', createDrinkStand] (the lesson id is 'drink-stand'); in src/config/lesson.js set that lesson available: true and add a UI.drinkStand block with ALL new Japanese strings. No UI text hardcoded elsewhere. Customer answers come only from answerFor(LESSON, drinkId).

Stand and camera per SPEC 6: fixed camera high and behind the player (use cameraRig with a fixed target/preset; no follow drift, no free exploration). Top: three serving windows with customers facing the camera. Middle: the avatar (characters.create({ model: characters.playerModel })) in a small clamped work area behind the counter. Bottom, nearest the camera: six large drink stations in a row, each a distinct procedural object plus a sign (CanvasTexture) with a drink picture and the English word. Everything must be visible without overlap at 1366x768 and still readable at 1280x720.

Drink looks (SPEC 6): water clear pale blue, milk white, orange juice orange, apple juice pale gold with an apple mark, tea amber with a teacup, soda bright green and fizzy (melon soda). Distinct at a glance.

Controls per SPEC 6: WASD/arrows walk inside the work area with the Restaurant's movement feel (copy its updateMovement: heading atan2(move.x, -move.y), shortest-way turning). Generous proximity zones for stations and windows. Space at a station pours (same pour time for every drink, about 1 s, with a visible cup of that liquid in the avatar's hands; pouring while holding empties the old cup first). Space at an asked customer while holding a cup serves. At an unasked customer the talk prompt appears via promptQuestion(ctx, LESSON, { isActive, onAccepted }) from src/systems/speechPrompt.js. Clicking/tapping a station or customer (raycast) makes the avatar walk there by itself and perform the same action on arrival, so a trackpad alone can play the whole game.

Loop per SPEC 6: customer walks to a RANDOM free window; asked -> answers with answerFor(LESSON, drink) via ctx.dialogue (spoken + bubble), bubble then disappears; no ticket, icon, or persistent text of the order anywhere. Right drink -> emote-yes, happy Japanese line, customer leaves, next arrives. Wrong drink -> polite Japanese refusal with NO English repeat, cup emptied, customer stays, patience keeps running.

Listening again (SPEC 3): the shared createListenAgain({ root, label: UI.listenAgain, onPress }) from src/ui/listenAgain.js is shown while the avatar is at an asked, unserved customer; pressing it replays that customer's exact answer sentence and marks that customer replayed. Never on Space, never deducts normal credit.

Difficulty per SPEC 6: customers per session L1 6 / L2 7 / L3 8; at most 1 / 2 / 3 at windows at once; overflow waits in a visible line, unasked, patience paused. RUSH finale: the last three customers arrive in quick succession with a large ラッシュ！ banner. Patience: visible generous meter above each customer at a window (tune around 50-60 s), paused while that customer's talk prompt is open; when empty the customer waves and leaves politely; play continues. No failure state anywhere.

Anti-shortcut per SPEC 6: each customer's drink is uniformly random over all six, independent of model, window, arrival order and other customers; repeats allowed. Station left-to-right order shuffled once per session. Nothing highlights the correct station, nothing is preselected, the avatar starts empty-handed, customers show nothing drink-related. Implement the random choices as pure seedable functions in scoring.js (e.g. pickDrink(rng), shuffleStations(rng)).

Customer models: Kenney keys not used elsewhere in play (the avatar is characters.playerModel 'a'; Restaurant uses e, f, i, j, m; Coloring uses b) — pick from the rest, randomly per customer. Do NOT tint textured Kenney models. Kenney models face +z at rotation.y = 0; customers at windows face the camera.

Scoring in scoring.js: pure scoreSession(records) where each record is { outcome: 'first' | 'later' | 'left', patienceLeft: 0..1, replayed: boolean } in serve order. Per customer: first-try 5, later 2, left 0; +2 * patienceLeft if served; +1 memory bonus if served and never replayed; +0.5 streak bonus for a first-try serve that extends a consecutive first-try streak to 2 or more. ratio = earned / maximum possible for the same number of customers. Stars: >= 0.75 -> 3, >= 0.4 -> 2, else 1; first-try share < 0.5 can never give 3 stars. Adjust the thresholds only if the tests below cannot all hold, and say so.

scoring.test.mjs must cover at least: all first-try with moderate patience (0.5) and no replays -> 3 stars; the same but every customer replayed -> still 3 stars; a seeded guessing simulation (random drink each attempt until right, over many sessions) reaches 3 stars in under 1% of sessions; first-try share below half never gives 3 stars; all customers left -> 1 star; streak bonus counts only consecutive first-try serves; pickDrink over several hundred seeded draws covers all six drinks; shuffleStations is a permutation.
Streak: show the current first-try streak as a small combo pop near the stand when it is 2 or more (Japanese text from UI.drinkStand).

Turnaround after the last customer: promptAnswer(ctx, LESSON, ...) with all six drinks, a warm reaction (e.g. the avatar receives a cup of the chosen drink), then finish({ stars, detail: { category: 'drink', answer } }). Frame the turnaround as a readable two-shot (the Coloring turnaround framing is a good reference).

Test hooks: stable DOM class names for the minigame's own overlay (at least an action/instruction element, the ラッシュ banner, the combo pop, the patience meters if DOM), and a READ-ONLY window.__eslDebug.drinkStand snapshot getter returning { phase, level, heldDrink, stations: [{ id, screen: {x, y} }], customers: [{ window, asked, served, screen: {x, y} }] } with screen positions projected to CSS pixels. It must NOT expose customers' wanted drinks. Remove it in exit().

exit() disposes every owned geometry, material, texture and canvas, removes overlays, listeners, injected styles and the debug hook, and clears speech/hud targets, exactly as the Restaurant does. Entering Drink Stand twice from the hub must not leak or duplicate anything.
npm test and npm run build must both pass.
constraints: Do NOT modify SPEC.md, src/systems/*, src/ui/*, src/scenes/hub.js, src/styles.css, the Restaurant, Coloring or the placeholder. If a shared system genuinely lacks something, say so in the summary instead of editing it. The only shared edits allowed: the registry line and import in src/main.js, and in src/config/lesson.js the drink-stand `available` flag plus a new UI.drinkStand block.
Do NOT add dependencies. three and vite only.
Do NOT build Sports or Zoo, a universal minigame base class, or shared scoring maths with other minigames.
No mouse-look, pointer lock or manual camera rotation.

Source-edit hygiene: edit files with structured file tools. If a shell-based edit fails on quoting or escaping, stop editing through the shell for that change and use the file tools; never escalate through nested shell/python/regex patches.
Do not inline code into shell commands; run the declared npm scripts.
notes: Governing rule (SPEC): the NPC's English answer must be information the child needs. For Drink Stand: a child who ignores 'I like milk.' can still finish (trial and error, never stuck) but can never reliably get three stars. In your summary, state how each anti-shortcut leak in SPEC was checked (fixed mapping, order, elimination, colour/appearance cues, default selection, free trial-and-error). Tone: the fast, arcade-like stage between calm Coloring and active Sports — bright, bouncy, snappy feedback, but generous patience; 8-year-olds on Chromebook trackpads. Known traps from earlier slices: Kenney models face +z; one avatar key; tinting textured Kenney models turns skin grey; the dialogue bubble uses width max-content; focused buttons must not swallow movement keys (already handled in input.js); keep every clickable thing keyboard-reachable. Restaurant is the closest reference for movement, proximity actions, dialogue anchoring, patience, and exit() hygiene; Coloring for the turnaround two-shot and listen-again use. Append meaningful design decisions to DESIGN_DECISIONS.md as dated entries. List every file you touched.
